correctness.rationale: The two half-plane geometric expansions of the reciprocal sine product give an exact boundary-value formula for the Fourier transform. For odd factor count the transform is the boundary jump, so only residues survive; for even factor count it is the boundary sum, leaving a nonzero regular term off the poles. Quadratic-irrational ratios give a uniform order-one-over-k Diophantine lower bound and hence polynomial coefficient growth. The weighted-simplex count gives the stated density. The sign and normalization recover the published three-factor delta-second-derivative and delta coefficients exactly.

value.rationale: The result is not a routine parameter increment: it identifies the structural mechanism that decides whether the Fourier side is discrete at all. The parity of the number of sine factors switches the boundary combination from a jump, which localizes on poles, to a sum, which leaves a nonzero regular component. This both generates an explicit hierarchy of odd polynomial density orders with higher delta derivatives and proves a sharp obstruction for every even order in the same natural family. That distinction directly organizes and limits the recent three-factor construction.
